question: Two engineers on the same team report that Claude behaves inconsistently: one gets careful adherence to a 'always run the linter before committing' rule, while the other says Claude never mentions the linter at all, even in the same repository on the same branch. Before assuming the rule text is unclear, what is the fastest way to confirm whether the inconsistency is actually a memory-loading problem?
options: A) Have each engineer run /memory and compare which CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and rules files are loaded to see if the linter rule is missing
B) Compare the two engineers' Claude Code version numbers, since instruction-following is versioned per release and needs a version match
C) Ask both engineers to restart their machines, since CLAUDE.md changes only take effect after a full operating system reboot occurs
D) Have each engineer delete their local git history and re-clone the repository, since stale git objects usually cause instruction drift between machines
correct_answers: A) Have each engineer run /memory and compare which CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and rules files are loaded to see if the linter rule is missing
explanations: Correct. /memory lists exactly which CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and rules files are loaded in the current session; if the linter instruction is missing from one engineer's list, that immediately isolates the problem to a loading/scoping issue rather than instruction wording.
Version mismatches could cause differences, but comparing versions doesn't reveal what's actually loaded, and instruction-following isn't gated by a required version match for diagnosis.
CLAUDE.md files are read fresh at the start of each session; no OS reboot is required or relevant to whether an instruction is loaded.
Stale git objects do not affect which memory files Claude Code discovers and loads, and re-cloning is a disruptive step with no diagnostic value here.
